title: Invariance under state equality
statement: Fix a Boolean oracle on four indices and finite Boolean strings, an input string, a natural-number register bound $B$, a control label $l$, and a proposition $P$. If two counting-algorithm states $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are equal, and the abstract machine starting at $l$ with register vector from $\sigma'$ terminates with all registers at most $B$ and accepts if and only if $P$ holds, then the same bounded termination and acceptance property holds when it starts with the register vector from $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean oracle on four indices and finite Boolean strings
The machine property for $\sigma'$: bounded termination and acceptance equivalent to $P$
replaced:
Let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each finite Boolean
string, and fix an input string, a natural-number register bound, a machine label, and a
proposition. For states $\sigma,\sigma'$ of the machine, if $\sigma=\sigma'$ and the
machine starting at label $l$ with state $\sigma'$ terminates while keeping every
register at most $B$, and accepts if and only if $P$ holds, then the same bounded
termination and acceptance property holds with initial state $\sigma$.
